frameworks.title: Political
frameworks.assessment: Airspace access and geopolitical shocks constrain networks; a geopolitical driver is not an enterprise procurement.

frameworks.title: Economic
frameworks.assessment: Thin forecast margins amplify fuel exposure and utilisation trade-offs. Market size is not addressable IT spend.

frameworks.title: Social
frameworks.assessment: High travel volumes coexist with service and accessibility expectations; do not assume willingness to pay for AI.

frameworks.title: Technological
frameworks.assessment: Existing operational AI and conversational distribution suggest integration and outcome questions rather than greenfield platforms.

frameworks.title: Legal
frameworks.assessment: Safety assurance and flight-specific passenger rights constrain automation and disruption workflows.

frameworks.title: Environmental
frameworks.assessment: Fuel mandates create chain-of-custody and assurance interfaces; fuel suppliers and airline responsibilities differ.

frameworks.title: Rivalry
frameworks.assessment: Strong: low-cost and network carriers compete on overlapping journeys; no route-level intensity quantified.

frameworks.title: Buyer power
frameworks.assessment: Material: travellers compare offers and service. Actual elasticity and channel switching need evidence.

frameworks.title: Supplier power
frameworks.assessment: Material dependencies on airframes, fuel, airports and maintenance; named technology relationships need scope confirmation.

frameworks.title: New entrants
frameworks.assessment: Fleet capital, operational approvals and network access constrain entry; not proof of no new competition.

frameworks.title: Substitutes
frameworks.assessment: Rail, remote meetings and alternative destinations are plausible substitutes; affected routes and switching remain research gaps.
